# dsh-screenshoot
A DSH plugin for screen and window captures. Cross-platform: Windows, macOS, Linux (X11).

The main difference from an ordinary "screen screenshot": a window is captured **by its own
pixels**

, so the shot works even if the window is behind another window, minimized in the
background or out

of focus. A movie in the foreground and the agent's app behind it are not
a problem.
## Tools
| Tool | What it does |

| `screen_monitors` | list of monitors: position, size, scale, primary |
| `screen_windows` | visibl

e windows: id, pid, title, process, position, size |
| `screen_capture_monitor` | capture of a whole

monitor |
| `screen_capture_region` | capture of a rectangular region |
| `screen_capture_window` |
capture of a window by `pid`, `title` or `id` (decimal or `0x…`) |

A region is clipped to the virtual desktop bounds: if it goes beyond the screen, the shot is
taken o

ver the intersection and `clamped` appears in the caption, and if there is no
intersection at all, a
clear error with the desktop dimensions is returned.

All three captures have `delayMs` — wait before the shot (up to 30 s). Useful when a menu
opens, an
animation is playing, or the window has not repainted yet.

All shots are saved as PNG and the path is returned in the result — it can be opened with the
`read_
image` tool to look at the picture.
## Window crop

A window can be captured not whole but with a rectangle cut out relative to its top-left
corner:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Coordinates are counted from the window corner (the top-left point of the content), not from
the scr

een. If the rectangle goes beyond the shot, an error with the picture dimensions is
returned — we wi
ll not silently clip to the edge.

Cropping works on every platform: the shot is taken the platform way, then the PNG is cropped
by the
built-in decoder (`src/png.js`), without ImageMagick and without external dependencies.
## Shots in chat

Like in Browser: after a shot a thumbnail appears in the tool row. The host raises a local
frame ser
ver on `127.0.0.1:49231`, the tool returns a `[shot:]` marker, and the client renders an ``
from it. The last 24 frames are kept in memory; the files stay on disk.
Clicking a thumbnail opens the PNG in a new tab.
## How it works per platform
**Windows** — PowerShell + Win32:

- `EnumWindows` + `DwmGetWindowAttribute` — window list and exact bounds;
- `PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFU

LLCONTENT)` — rendering the window into a bitmap instead of copying
the screen; that is exactly why

awareness — coordinates and sizes in physical pixels (important at 200 %).
- Window titles are passe
d as base64, and stdout is forced to UTF-8 — otherwise Cyrillic breaks.
**macOS** — `screencapture` + JavaScript for Automation:
-l <window id>` — a window, even an occluded one; `-R` — region; `-D` — monitor.

The **Screen Recording** permission is required (System Settings → Privacy). Without it macOS
will o
nly give the wallpaper.
**Linux (X11)** — `xrandr`, `wmctrl`, ImageMagick `import`:
— the window from its own buffer; `-window root -crop` — region.

On Wayland the X11 tools do not see windows: the plugin will honestly say what is missing
instead of
a black shot. Wayland needs a portal/grim approach.

and restart DSH. The plugin pulls no npm dependencies — only the platform's system tools.
## Languages
Interface languages: Russian, English, Chinese.

The interface language comes from the `language` extension setting when it is `ru`, `en` or
`zh`. Th

e value `auto` follows the application language: `document.documentElement.lang`, then
`navigator.la

nguage`; `ru*` → `ru`, `zh*` → `zh`, otherwise `en`. With no setting at all the
default is `ru`.

The setting is changed in the plugin form **Plugins → Screenshoot** and stored in the file
`%LOCALAP
PDATA%\dsh-screenshoot\settings.json`.
